notes: The materially different alternative gives *may hurt* and *may profit* to the two `לְ`s as rule 49 result frames. It is not taken because those verbs introduce an event and an affected object the Hebrew does not predicate, which is the boundary rule 20 draws against a supplied lexical verb; the ASV's italics corroborate without deciding, by rule 7.
Both `לְ`s are unrepresented under rule 40, since the ASV promotes each object to the direct object of the supplied verb and spends no word on the preposition's own relation.
`כְּמוֹ` is the predicate of the recast clause *as thou art* and carries the construction-supplied copula under rule 49, discontinuous around the suffix's *thou*.
